artifact_policy.authoritative_results: Only artifacts marked validated may support research claims.
artifact_policy.row_level_requirement: Every aggregate must be reproducible from saved row-level predictions.
artifact_policy.legacy_outputs: Existing output files are retained for forensic comparison and are not citable.

entries.reason: Regression test proves stores loaded from different graph paths are independent.
Regression tests prove concurrent transient contexts are isolated and claim scores are local to verification calls.
The artifact lacks paired baseline predictions, does not include the reported RMIT control, and predates graph-store isolation fixes.
Routing modes now execute distinct policies, but the saved artifact predates the fix and conditions still require cached decomposition and linking for a valid paired comparison.
The experiment returned fixed constants rather than measurements.
Coverage, selective accuracy, AURC, and tie fractions were generated from formulas or unsupported report tables.
Synthetic confidence features were sampled conditionally on gold correctness and fallback records were artificially separable.
The benchmark contains synthetic individual claims derived from the verification graph, not set-valued advising answers.
Records marked held out do not remove the true edge from the graph used by verification.
The candidate has deterministic KG-derived expected sets and entity-grouped splits, but only one advising intent, 50 source courses, template responses, and no independent advisor audit.

Paired test rows, five zero-fixed-point within-relation derangements, an empty-graph control, hashes, and subject-clustered intervals are recorded. The 100% baseline is circular because synthetic gold labels and predictions share the same deterministic expected-set query, so only graph-destruction sensitivity is currently informative.

All 50 cached handbook sources are linked. The chosen design has one reviewer, so it supports source audit and corrections but not inter-annotator agreement. Twenty calibration/test courses are required before dataset revision.

Row-level predictions are saved for every cell and all aggregates are recomputed from them by scripts/summarize_rerun_results.py. The FactKG cells are not citable: a name-shadowing defect at verification_pipeline.py:305 raised TypeError on 22.6 percent of azure-4.1-mini rows and 6.0 percent of gemma-4-e4b rows, and eval_harness substitutes the majority class for each crash, so reported FactKG accuracy is inflated and the true value is only bounded within [59.2, 81.4] percent. RMIT and CoDEx cells completed without crashes but inherit the existing benchmark-validity limits: RMIT gold labels are graph-derived and circular, and CoDEx retains the invalidated_heldout_edges_present finding. Intervals are IID row bootstraps, not clustered, because the saved rows carry no subject-entity field.

stage_3_map_claim_to_triple defined a local helper named mapped on line 268 and rebound the same name to a boolean on line 305 inside the unclassified-relation fallback, so every later return mapped(...) raised TypeError: 'bool' object is not callable. Reproduced deterministically with a stub LLM. Repaired by renaming the boolean to relation_was_mapped; StageThreeFallbackTests added to cover the fallback path; suite went from 23 to 25 passing tests. The post-fix sweep shows zero crashes across all six cells and no previously-masked exception. Because every exit path from the branch called mapped(), the zero pre-fix crash count on RMIT and CoDEx proves the branch never executed there, so the repair cannot have altered those datasets.

On any exception both harnesses substituted the dataset default label (Contradicted on FactKG, Not-in-KG otherwise) and scored it as a prediction. Because Contradicted is also FactKG's majority class, 113 crashes were scored as 111 correct predictions. Repaired: a crash now leaves the row unscored (pred null, raw_pred 'Error', plus the exception text) and compute_metrics excludes unscored rows from the denominator, returning n_scored so the caller can see the gap. Output JSON carries n_scored and n_unscored_errors. Covered by CrashScoringTests.

Stage 3 substituted the resolved entity KEY for a claim's object on every open-domain relation. Entity records are keyed by id (Q-id on CoDEx) while their field values are surface labels: data/codex_graph.json holds 17203 object values, all labels and zero Q-ids. Stage 4 therefore compared an id against a label and reported a value mismatch for every true claim, driving CoDEx Supported recall to 0.039 while Contradicted became the default answer at precision 0.374. Repaired by projecting a resolved object back to its stored label before returning. Measured on the asserted-triple oracle parse (n=496, no LLM): accuracy 0.4435 to 0.6915 with Supported recall 0.071 to 1.000. Covered by ObjectNamespaceTests.

link_entity accepted a bi-encoder cosine match at 0.35, so subjects absent from the graph were linked to their nearest neighbour instead of being reported unresolved; all 97 genuinely-absent CoDEx subjects in the first 500 rows were linked to a wrong entity. The threshold is now a constructor parameter (default 0.35, preserving RMIT behaviour) and the token-overlap fallback is gated so it cannot undo a rejection. Selected on a held-out split (dev = CoDEx rows 500-1000, test = rows 0-500): the sweep is monotone, dev selects 0.95, and dev 0.8435 generalizes to test 0.8206 against 0.4798 at the library default 0.35 (measured on the code as shipped, with all five repairs in place). Remains candidate because it is calibrated on one graph and one benchmark.

verify_statement combined claim verdicts by priority with no distinction between 'the graph lacks this fact' and 'this claim could not be linked'. LLM decomposition routinely emits one good claim plus a fragment ('The member', 'languages of X'); the fragment resolved to entity_unresolved, voted Not-in-KG, and overrode the correctly-verified claim. Claims whose subject could not be linked are now recorded with voted=false and withheld from the vote unless every claim is unresolved, in which case the subject genuinely is absent and Not-in-KG stands. Found by smoke-testing the end-to-end path after the threshold change; the oracle-parse diagnostic could not surface it because it supplies exactly one gold claim per row. MEASURED AND DISABLED BY DEFAULT. Paired ablations on identical rows with concurrent arms: on RMIT n=300 gemma-4-e4b the rule is the sole cause of a reproducible regression on the existence slice, 29/50 off versus 21/50 on, costing 2.67 points overall and matching the pre-repair 29/50 exactly when disabled. On CoDEx n=250 gemma-4-e4b it gains only 0.80 points (77.60 to 78.40) with 18 of 250 predictions differing, a 7.2 percent disagreement identical to that cell's measured run-to-run flip rate, so the gain is not distinguishable from noise. Shipping a change whose only measurable effect is a regression is not defensible, so withhold_unresolved_claims defaults to False and the behaviour is retained behind a flag. The rule remains semantically correct; the RMIT cost traces to a separate decomposition bug in the coordinator-existence generator, which extracts 'RMIT catalogue' as the subject. Re-measure D4 after that decomposition is fixed.

The open-domain relation-mapping fallback fired only when the relation was literally 'unclassified' or empty. LLM decomposition instead emits concrete but non-canonical surface phrasings ('is member of' against a graph field named 'member of political party'), so stage 4 fell through to 'Unrecognized relation class' and returned Not-in-KG for facts the graph holds. The fallback now also fires when the relation is neither an ontology relation nor a field on the resolved subject's record. ONTOLOGY_RELATIONS exempts the RMIT dispatch path, which is unaffected.

Post-fix sweep over RMIT n=300, FactKG n=500, CoDEx n=500 for azure-4.1-mini and google/gemma-4-e4b, plus the deterministic graph-destruction control. All exit codes 0, zero crashes, row-level predictions saved, and every aggregate recomputed from those rows by scripts/summarize_rerun_results.py. Not promoted to validated: RMIT gold labels are circular because eval_rmit.py verifies a template string interpolated from the fields the verifier queries; CoDEx retains the invalidated_heldout_edges_present finding; FactKG collapses Not-in-KG into Contradicted so abstention cannot be scored; intervals are IID row bootstraps rather than clustered because the rows carry no subject-entity field; sampling is by prefix rather than random; and a single run per cell is inadequate given a measured 5.75 percent mean prediction flip rate between identical reruns.

Ten cells (2 engines x RMIT n=300, plus FactKG and CoDEx n=500 under both prefix and random sampling) run against shipped defaults after repairing four defects and measuring a fifth (D4) that ships disabled. All exit codes 0, zero unscored rows, row-level predictions saved, every aggregate recomputed from those rows, complete 10-cell process manifest. With sampling held constant CoDEx moves 41.80 to 81.80 percent (azure-4.1-mini) and 37.20 to 75.80 percent (gemma-4-e4b), and Supported recall moves 0.039 to 0.981. RMIT azure-4.1-mini is unchanged at 97.33 percent. Not promoted to validated: two runs per cell against a measured 5.07 percent mean prediction flip rate, so nothing below about 2.5 points is resolvable and the FactKG before/after deltas of +3.4 and +2.8 are directional only; RMIT gold labels remain circular; intervals are IID row bootstraps rather than clustered because rows still carry no subject-entity field; confidence remains uncalibrated; and the entity-link threshold is calibrated on CoDEx only.

Graph-destruction control run against the LLM pipeline's verification path (stages 3-4, no LLM, deterministic) on CoDEx, which the 2026-07-25 study listed as never run. Within-relation shuffling preserves entity set, relation keys and per-relation value multiset while destroying subject-value association. Before the stage-3 object-namespace repair the control changed 1.8 to 2.8 percent of predictions; after it changes 27.2 to 30.9 percent (mean 28.9) with accuracy falling from 82.06 to 56.1-60.5 percent, and removing all relations collapses the pipeline to 35.89 percent, the majority floor. This answers RQ1 affirmatively for the LLM pipeline on CoDEx. The script exits non-zero below --min_change_rate so it can gate future changes. Candidate because it covers one graph and one benchmark.

data/factkg_test.jsonl is sorted into 45 contiguous reasoning-type blocks, so data[:500] selects 2 of 13 reasoning types (existence 375, num1|substitution 125) at a majority floor of 0.6460 against the full 9041-row set's 0.5135. Running both sampling arms on identical code gives 81.40 versus 58.60 percent (azure-4.1-mini) and 84.60 versus 57.80 percent (gemma-4-e4b), a gap of 23 to 27 points attributable to the sample alone. The per-type breakdown shows reasoning type determines the gold label almost deterministically: every *|substitution type is about 100 percent Contradicted and every plain numN type about 98 percent Supported, so the pipeline's Contradicted prior scores 0.94-1.00 on one group and 0.03-0.33 on the other. eval_harness now defaults to --sample random and records the seed. This is a measured instance of the C3 binary-benchmark trap.

Paired pre-fix and post-fix runs under identical settings, restricted to the four cells where the repair is provably unreachable, flip 2.0 to 9.6 percent of individual predictions (mean 5.75 percent) while accuracy moves at most 2.0 points. Aggregate stability therefore understates instability, and single-run engine comparisons below roughly 2 points are not resolvable. The --seed flag in eval_rmit.py seeds only Python's random module and does not constrain LLM sampling.
The runner combined invalidated experiments and inserted hand-written p-values.

The script did not evaluate any baseline. closed_book_llm_accuracy, context_llm_with_abstain_accuracy and nli_verbalized_triples_accuracy were hard-coded constants (0.52/0.72/0.74 for FactKG, 0.35/0.42/0.45 for CoDEx and MetaQA, 0.50/0.88/0.90 for catalog2) selected by dataset name, and the NLI arm named a model that exists nowhere in the codebase. Only majority_class_accuracy and stratified_random_accuracy were computed from data. Script and standalone artifact deleted; recoverable from git history. No report ever quoted these values. Real baselines must be measured through eval_harness.py --method {closed_book_llm,context_llm,pipeline}, which already implements the first two, and must emit row-level predictions.

scripts/convert_codex.py:178-185 and scripts/convert_metaqa.py:175-178 inject RMIT course scaffolding into every public-benchmark entity record: course_id, title, prerequisites=[], credits=12, school='Science', coordinator='Unknown', coordinator_email='Unknown'. Verified constant across all 1182 CoDEx entities. Leonhard Euler is therefore recorded as a 12-credit course in the School of Science. Consequences: (1) estimate_relation_occupancy returns a fabricated 1.0 for hasCreditValue, partOfSchool and requiresPrerequisite on CoDEx and MetaQA, contaminating any dynamic-routing arm measured on those graphs; (2) a claim the mapper routes to a course-shaped relation is compared against a converter constant, a spurious agreement channel; (3) these four fields are invariant under the value-shuffling destruction control, so they cannot register a prediction change and dilute the measured grounding rate. Fixing the converters changes both graphs and therefore invalidates the current CoDEx/MetaQA results, which is why this is filed as an open defect rather than silently repaired.

entries.reason_note: Retained after the 2026-07-26 regeneration: the rebuilt RMIT set is still 300/300 questions in `text`, because the generator's paraphrase prompt asks for 'a natural-sounding query, question, or statement'.
entries.reason: The standing de-circularization recommendation carried in rerun_20260726_paper.md:450, rerun_20260725_paper.md:617 and comprehensive_report_20260725.md:613 — 'verify text rather than raw_claim' — is not implementable as written. All 300 rows of data/rmit_test_set.jsonl carry a question in `text` ('How many credit points is Course 038974 worth?') and the assertion in `raw_claim` ('Course 038974 is worth 12 credit points'), despite input_type='response'. The pipeline verifies claims, so submitting `text` yields Out-of-scope with zero decomposed claims: measured 3/3 rows under google/gemma-4-e4b via --verify_field text. De-circularization therefore requires authoring natural-language *responses* whose surface form does not derive from graph field names (E1/RMIT-NL); switching fields cannot substitute for it. The --verify_field flag is retained to make this measurable and to keep the claim honest. MEASURED AT FULL SCALE 2026-07-26 (nusmods_institutional_benchmark): all 300 rows under google/gemma-4-e4b, zero unscored. raw_claim 89.67% vs text 45.33%, paired McNemar p=6.2e-39. The 44.33-point drop is NOT a circularity estimate: 152/300 rows (50.67%) return Out-of-scope with zero decomposed claims -- the pipeline correctly refuses a question -- and are scored as errors only because no gold label exists for 'no claim present'. On the 148 rows where a claim was extractable, accuracy is 91.89%, slightly above the raw_claim arm. Artifacts: output/experiments/nusmods_20260726/ablation/rmit__gemma_4_e4b__{raw_claim,text}.json.

Both converters built their entity list with list(set(...)) and then called random.shuffle() under random.seed(42). Set iteration order over strings varies per process under Python's hash randomization, so the seed never controlled the 70/30 active/held-out split: two consecutive runs produced different graphs, different test sets, and different entity counts. convert_codex.py also picked the Contradicted arm's mutated object with random.choice() over an unordered set difference. Fixed by sorting before shuffling and before choosing. Verified: two consecutive runs of convert_codex.py now produce byte-identical data/codex_graph.json (sha256 b41be479f3601b61) and data/codex_test.jsonl (sha256 0a9198e01b4339c1). data/metaqa_test.jsonl remains irreproducible by construction because convert_metaqa.py verbalizes claims through an LLM; only its graph is deterministic.

Two defects. (1) The generator called random.choices() a dozen times with no random.seed() anywhere, so every run drew a different 300 rows and no RMIT number could be tied to a reproducible sample; a --seed argument now controls row selection. (2) paraphrase_claim() fell back to the raw claim only on exception, so an empty completion was written into the dataset verbatim: a regeneration against google/gemma-4-e4b left 208 of 300 rows with an empty `text` field, and after adding empty-detection a further run still fell back to the template on 183 of 300 rows (61% empty-completion rate on that engine). The paraphrase now retries once and falls back explicitly. The shipped set was regenerated with provider=azure, model=azure-4.1-mini: 300 rows, 0 empty, 0 fallbacks, stratification preserved (one-hop 100 / conjunction 50 / existence 50 / multi-hop 50 / negation 50; Supported 125 / Contradicted 125 / Not-in-KG 50). Row selection is reproducible under the seed; the paraphrased surface form is not, since it is generated at temperature 0.7.

First sweep against the de-scaffolded public graphs, the absence-dispatched stage-4 accessors, and the regenerated RMIT set. Supersedes rerun_20260726_final, whose CoDEx and MetaQA numbers were measured against contaminated graphs and whose RMIT rows no longer exist. Not comparable row-for-row with any earlier run: the CoDEx graph moved from 1182 to 1189 entities, both public test sets were rebuilt, and the RMIT sample was redrawn under a seed for the first time. Engines: azure-4.1-mini and google/gemma-4-e4b. Occupancy gate after regeneration: CoDEx interior relations 18 -> 23 of 25, MetaQA 4 -> 3 of 6, RMIT unchanged at 0 of 7 (its saturation is genuine, not injected).

Institutional-catalog tri-state benchmark over the NUS module catalog (11,647 modules, AY2020-21..AY2025-26, NUSMods v2 API), plus a full two-engine study with an ablation suite. Built to remove the circularity that invalidates eval_rmit.py: every gold label is world-assumption-independent, verified empirically -- forcing fixed_owa changes 0 of 500 predictions and fixed_cwa changes 1, and that 1 is a decomposition-unstable row that flips under an unrelated flag too. The benchmark is therefore deliberately blind to C1. Gates: graph-destruction 0.2907 mean prediction change (gate 0.20, PASS); stage-3/4 ceiling 1.0000 at entity_link_threshold 0.95 vs 0.7520 at 0.35 and 0.60, where the Not-in-KG class collapses to 0.248 recall. Results, n=500, identical rows, zero unscored rows in every cell: pipeline 99.80% (azure-4.1-mini) / 99.40% (gemma-4-e4b), context_llm 90.80% / 72.00%, closed_book_llm 41.00% / 33.80% against a 33.80% majority floor. Headline finding is the engine gap: 18.80 points on the context baseline (paired McNemar p=9.5e-24) vs 0.40 points inside the pipeline (p=0.625, n.s.). Advantage over the context baseline is concentrated in closed-world set reasoning (prerequisite-negation 100% vs 66%). Ablations: link threshold is the only consequential knob (-25.00 points at 0.35 and 0.60, both engines); routing, unresolved-claim withholding, and a same-seed replicate all move 0-1 rows. Run-to-run flip rate 0.10% (2 flips over 2,000 row-executions). Candidate, not validated: Supported items remain template-derived from the queried fields, the headline sits at the stage-4 ceiling so the benchmark discriminates poorly among competent systems, the ontology is three relations, and confidence is uncalibrated so no false-contradiction rate is controlled.
